item.title: BBC joins paramedics on duty in Lebanon after Israeli strikes
item.summary: BBC Middle East correspondent Hugo Bachega joins paramedics on duty in Nabatieh - a city that was once vibrant, but is now abandoned.

item.title: Iran carried out highest number of executions in decades
item.summary: Organisations warn many more people could be executed in the wake of the anti-government protests which swept Iran earlier this year.

item.title: Hungary's next PM would pick up if Putin calls and tell him to stop Ukraine war
item.summary: Russia has offered "pragmatic" relations, but Péter Magyar says he will not call Vladimir Putin himself.

item.title: Peru election drags into second day after ballot delivery fiasco
item.summary: Technical and logistical problems mean Peruvians choosing a new president and members of Congress continue to vote on Monday.

item.title: Nigeria Air Force orders investigation after dozens killed in airstrike
item.summary: There are reports that more than 100 people were killed, although the authorities have not commented.

item.title: Lebanon seeks peace, but Hezbollah needs to be convinced first
item.summary: The Lebanese government go into peace talks with limited influence over the group.

item.title: Hospital at centre of child HIV outbreak caught reusing syringes in undercover filming
item.summary: Footage shows staff injecting without gloves and reusing syringes, but the hospital boss refuses to acknowledge it is genuine.

item.title: Italian PM condemns ally Trump over 'unacceptable' Pope criticism
item.summary: Italy's prime minister and the US president are close allies, but Trump has refused to apologise to the "very weak" Pope Leo XIV.

item.title: Britney Spears goes into rehab after driving under the influence arrest
item.summary: The singer voluntarily checks herself into a treatment facility, three weeks before her court date.

item.title: Philippines accuses Chinese fishermen of dumping cyanide in South China Sea
item.summary: Beijing rejects the allegation as a "farce", while Manila claims the poison was used to kill fish and deprive troops stationed in the area of food.
